title: Essential surjectivity of the discrete representation to internal group functor
statement: For every topological group $G$ and carrier universe $w$, equip $\mathcal C=\mathrm{DiscreteContAction}(\mathrm{Type}(w),G)$ with a Cartesian monoidal structure and braiding. The functor $H$ of [def-exc-discrete-continuous-rep-to-commgrp] is essentially surjective: every internal commutative group object $A$ is isomorphic to $H(M)$ for some discrete continuous integer representation $M$.

proof.text: Construct the binary carrier product with diagonal action. Its stabilizers are intersections of two open stabilizers, so it is a discrete continuous action. The projection pair identifies it with the given Cartesian tensor product; on carriers the comparison map is bijective. Construct the singleton trivial action and compare it with the terminal tensor unit. These comparisons prove that the faithful forgetful functor F to types preserves finite products.

Use Mathlib Functor.Monoidal.ofChosenFiniteProducts, Functor.Braided.ofChosenFiniteProducts, and F.mapCommGrp to transport the internal commutative group A to its carrier. CommGrpTypeEquivalenceCommGrp.commGrpCommGroup gives the concrete commutative group law. For each g, the action maps form a natural transformation F to itself; mapCommGrpNatTrans transports it to a group homomorphism. Passing to Additive and toIntLinearMap constructs an integer representation. The original action equations give its representation equations. The original continuous discrete action gives open stabilizers.

The carrier isomorphism from the constructed representation to A is the identity function. For the reverse functor of def-exc-discrete-continuous-rep-to-commgrp, the reconstructed unit and multiplication are pointwise zero and addition. Apply the faithful F to their compatibility equations. Functor.map_one and Functor.map_mul for the original internal group, followed by evaluation and the product projection identities, prove these equations. CommGrp.mkIso upgrades this now operation-preserving carrier isomorphism to an internal group isomorphism, giving essential surjectivity.

proof_origin.note: Second reader J3: complete explicit construction; finite-product comparisons and native group transport use the named Mathlib declarations, with no new assumptions or split-off statements.
